items.claim: The frozen-format test 'ignores the reserved action bit when decoding' still expects bit 2 to decode as nothing. To keep it passing, decodeInputs sets `action` as a non-enumerable property. Any spread, structuredClone or JSON.stringify of a decoded frame drops the action without a sound, which is a trap for the next night that copies or records replay inputs (for example B13 rival boosts).
items.evidence: tests/sim/replay.test.ts:63-66 `it('ignores the reserved action bit when decoding', () => { const text = bytesToBase64(Uint8Array.from([0x00, 0b111])); expect(decodeInputs(text, 1, 1)).toEqual([[{ steer: 0, throttle: true, brake: true }]]); });`. Since B12, bit 2 is a live flag: src/sim/replay.ts:6 'bit2 action (fire the power-up…)' and :26 `const FLAG_ACTION = 4;`. The workaround is src/sim/replay.ts:96-98: `// Non-enumerable, so frames still deep-equal what pre-pickup decoders gave (bit 2 used to be ignored) while input.action reads true and stepWorld fires.` `if ((flags & FLAG_ACTION) !== 0) Object.defineProperty(input, 'action', { value: true, writable: true, configurable: true });`. It is the only defineProperty in src/. The behaviour is already pinned through the public value by tests/sim/pickup-replay.test.ts:21-34, which checks `decoded?.[0]?.action` is true and that 'action' is not in frames with bit 2 clear.
items.suggestedFix: Owner: change replay.test.ts:65 to expect `{ steer: 0, throttle: true, brake: true, action: true }` (or delete the case, since pickup-replay AC6 covers it). Then replace the defineProperty at replay.ts:96-98 with a plain `input.action = true` and drop the comment. stepWorld reads `input.action` the same way, so replays and bot laps don't change.

items.claim: Every car makes a new TrackPos object on every sim tick. stepCars sets `car.pos = trackPosition(...)`, and trackPosition gets its result from nearestLocal→projectOnSegment, which returns a fresh object literal. When a car is off the track, nearestGlobal (called from trackPosition and from surfaceAt) allocates one or two more. The old car.pos is thrown away right after: nothing keeps a reference to it between ticks.
items.evidence: src/sim/track.ts:491 `return { seg: i, s: ..., lateral, distance: Math.hypot(x - px, z - pz) };` (projectOnSegment, reached from nearestLocal:538 and nearestGlobal:505). src/sim/car.ts:290 `car.pos = trackPosition(track, car.x, car.z, car.pos);`, car.ts:291 surfaceAt → track.ts:566 `nearestGlobal(track, x, z).distance` (a TrackPos used for one field). Readers of car.pos all read it within the tick: world.ts:89/128/140 (`.s`), bot.ts:95-131 (`.seg`, `.s`, `.lateral`). No match in src/ for structuredClone or spreads of car/pos, and src/driver does not read pos. perf.json: the sim's other hot functions are allocation-free in source (scratch `hit`, `seg`, `ground`, `nearby`), so this is one of the few real per-tick allocation sites left on the stepCars path, at 6 cars × 60 Hz.
items.suggestedFix: Add an optional `out: TrackPos` parameter to projectOnSegment/nearestLocal/trackPosition, defaulting to a fresh object so the existing tests in tests/sim/track.test.ts:250-287 are unaffected. In trackPosition, write the local result into `prev` only after `prev.seg` has been read. Use one module scratch TrackPos for the global candidate and copy it into `out` only if it wins. In surfaceAt, use a scratch for the nearestGlobal distance check. Every number stays the same. Wait for in-flight PR #35, which also edits src/sim/car.ts.
